blocks.text: Wave pick design for building 2 dry

This is the working cut for PCF-TDD-2024-024 on March 7, 2024. Marcus Hale asked for a written bound after the current path (Mixed wave sizes, 40-90 lines, no cap) stopped being honest. I am Jeilen Jones, Order Picker, writing for Marcus Hale, Tasha Quinn, and Ben Crowe. Primary host wms.pinecrest.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on 90-line batch waves, then open questions. If you are on the floor next shift, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the steps.

Discrete pick, 24-line cap per tote. Batch pick only for single-SKU case-pick. Reject 90-line waves. I am not restating a hallway yes. 90-line batch waves is out because February 16 90-line wave made 11.4 lb totes and 6 pack backups. Tasha stopped it. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: cap=24, bad=90, lb=11.4, backup=6, weeks=4, totes=2.1, lines=38.6, sku=1. Sibling tickets PCF-1488 and PCF-REQ-2024-018. I will not reopen 90-line batch waves in a side thread because someone asked for a rate waiver. Tasha Quinn is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.
Decision for leadership

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Discrete pick, 24-line cap per tote. Batch pick only for single-SKU case-pick. Reject 90-line waves.

Background on wms.pinecrest.internal. Mixed wave sizes, 40-90 lines, no cap. That is the system Marcus Hale lives with, not a slide. I timed or pulled the leftover on rf.pinecrest.internal the week before this file. Miss counts, minutes, and weights in this file are from that pull, not a round number I liked. Ticket PCF-TDD-2024-024 names the pull. If those numbers moved after March 7, 2024, update this file in review, do not 'correct' them in a group chat.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Ben Crowe owns a leftover that is easy to skip: pack.pinecrest.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (07): refuse on 90-line batch waves, lock is 24-line cap, discrete, case-pick exception. I will not hide a process change inside a 'quick align' on PCF-1488.
A 90-line wave is not faster. It is a heavier tote and a slower pack.

What a skeptical lead would try first on wms.pinecrest.internal: the path Marcus Hale actually has, not an empty-tote photo. Metric I will argue is a clean confirm, not a vanity units-per-hour. If we cannot show that path on rf.pinecrest.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Jeilen Jones will not accept a hallway yes as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

blocks.label: Lock
blocks.text: 24-line cap, discrete, case-pick exception Host wms.pinecrest.internal. Ticket PCF-1488. Acceptor Marcus Hale.

Open clock: 24-line cap, discrete, case-pick exception. If that clock collides with a safety lock, the date moves and the scope does not. Marcus Hale hears the new date on PCF-TDD-2024-024. I will not book a change in the last 40 minutes of a lock because it is 'just a rate.' A rate change is a change. Host if we have to prove a count: wms.pinecrest.internal.

What I will not claim in PCF-TDD-2024-024

I will not claim 90-line batch waves is impossible at another shop. I will claim we will not do it here. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host wms.pinecrest.internal.
First useful slice for PCF-1488

First useful is 24-line cap, discrete, case-pick exception, not a prettier board or a louder huddle. Marcus Hale sees that slice on wms.pinecrest.internal. If the slice needs a second process, that is a new ticket and Marcus Hale is in the thread. I will not hide it inside PCF-TDD-2024-024.
Photos, labels, and identifiers (07)

A photo for this work is a bin or a seal, not a customer's face. Tote IDs stay on PCF-TDD-2024-024. Pressure is not a reason to paste a phone number into the ticket. Jeilen Jones will bounce it. Host if we have to prove a redaction: pack.pinecrest.internal.
